title: Smart Attendance System via Facial Recognition
summary: An automated contactless attendance tracking pipeline powered by deep facial recognition models, anti-spoofing liveness detection, and instant faculty dashboard synchronization.
overview: The Smart Attendance System is an end-to-end computer vision solution engineered to replace manual roll calls and biometric fingerprint queues at Sri Shakthi Institute of Engineering and Technology. Using edge cameras deployed at lecture hall entryways, the system captures multiple faces in real-time, validates biological liveness against photo spoofing, matches embeddings against the student database with 99.4% accuracy, and updates the academic ERP in sub-second latency.
problem: Traditional roll-calling consumes 10 to 15 minutes of every 50-minute lecture hour, resulting in substantial loss of instructional time. Fingerprint scanners lead to physical bottlenecks, hygienic concerns in large student cohorts, and proxy attendance issues that undermine institutional academic audits.
solution: We designed an automated multi-camera surveillance pipeline leveraging RetinaFace for multi-scale face localization, coupled with an optimized ArcFace embedding backbone fine-tuned on South Asian facial feature variations. A spatial-temporal tracking module ensures students entering in groups are distinctly recognized, verified with flash-reflection liveness checks, and marked present without pausing.
objectives: Eliminate instructional time loss by completing classroom attendance in under 3 seconds per entry stream.
Achieve greater than 99% true-positive recognition accuracy while maintaining sub-0.1% false-acceptance rate.
Incorporate robust anti-spoofing algorithms to defeat printed 2D photos, digital screens, and 3D mask attacks.
Provide real-time telemetry and exportable reports directly to departmental faculty and administrative portals.

title: SIET Campus AI Assistant & Chatbot
summary: A multimodal Generative AI assistant featuring Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) over campus regulations, exam schedules, course materials, and administrative workflows.
overview: The SIET Campus AI Assistant is a specialized conversational agent built to provide instant, hallucination-resistant guidance to 6,000+ students, faculty members, and campus visitors. Leveraging open-source small language models, domain-specific semantic embedding pipelines, and dense vector index retrieval, it addresses academic regulations, fee deadlines, syllabus queries, bus routes, and lab safety protocols with verifiable citations.
problem: University administrative desks receive thousands of redundant queries every admission and examination cycle. Official circulars are dispersed across disparate PDF circulars, static portals, and departmental notice boards, resulting in missed academic deadlines and severe administrative overhead.
solution: We architected an enterprise RAG pipeline that continuously ingests university circulars, course handbooks, and faculty directories into a high-performance vector store. When a student poses a query in English, Tamil, or Hinglish, hybrid keyword-vector retrieval extracts relevant chunks, and a fine-tuned Mistral-7B model formulates concise, cited answers with zero hallucinations.
objectives: Deliver sub-800ms streaming responses for complex multi-part campus questions.
Support bilingual conversation with vernacular Tamil and code-switched queries.
Provide transparent source citations referencing specific institutional circulars and dates.
Integrate role-based authentication allowing students to query personalized academic transcripts.

title: Multimodal Early Disease Prediction Platform
summary: A clinical diagnostic decision support platform predicting cardiovascular and diabetic risks using ensemble gradient boosting, electronic health records, and explainable SHAP values.
overview: The Multimodal Early Disease Prediction Platform empowers rural primary health centers around Coimbatore by providing proactive, explainable risk assessments for cardiovascular diseases, Type-2 diabetes, and chronic kidney ailments. By fusing routine blood laboratory parameters with demographic markers, clinicians receive instant risk probabilities backed by local feature contribution charts.
problem: Chronic lifestyle diseases in rural communities are frequently diagnosed only after irreversible organ damage occurs. Specialist cardiologists and nephrologists are concentrated in urban medical complexes, leaving primary healthcare workers without diagnostic validation tools.
solution: We developed a calibrated ensemble framework combining XGBoost, LightGBM, and TabNet with differential privacy constraints. The platform presents a web and tablet interface where lab technicians input basic clinical profiles and receive an instant prognostic evaluation along with actionable SHAP explanations.
objectives: Achieve an ROC-AUC of greater than 0.93 across validated cardiovascular cohorts.
Provide model interpretability via Waterfall and Force plots so clinicians understand diagnostic reasoning.
Ensure complete HIPAA and Indian Digital Personal Data Protection Act compliance with on-premise inference.
Deliver a responsive tablet UI capable of offline caching in low-connectivity rural health camps.

title: Edge AI Real-Time Object Detection Platform
summary: Industrial safety and automated defect inspection deployed on NVIDIA Jetson embedded platforms with TensorRT optimization and sub-15ms inference latency.
overview: The Edge AI Object Detection Platform brings real-time neural inference out of costly cloud servers and directly into constrained embedded hardware. Developed for smart manufacturing and campus laboratory safety, the system reliably identifies PPE compliance, machinery overheating hazards, and micro-defects at line speed.
problem: Cloud-based video analytics incurs recurring network bandwidth overhead, high recurring operational costs, and latency spikes that make emergency shutdown triggers unreliable in critical environments.
solution: We converted state-of-the-art YOLOv8 architectures into FP16/INT8 TensorRT execution engines executed on Jetson Orin Nano modules. Custom memory pipelines minimize CPU-GPU memory copies, unlocking sustained 65 FPS processing with under 12W power consumption.
objectives: Achieve real-time performance (>60 FPS) on embedded ARM-based edge systems.
Detect factory safety infractions including lack of helmets, vests, and safety goggles.
Provide hardware-isolated dry contact relays for instant machine stoppage.

problem: Traditional institutional alerts only trigger after end-semester exam failures, by which point credit deficits and academic probation have already accumulated.
solution: We trained calibrated Random Forest and LightGBM models on historical cohorts, generating weekly proactive advisory flags for faculty mentors with actionable root cause summaries.
objectives: Provide early warnings at the 4th week of the semester, allowing 12 weeks of corrective tutoring.
Protect student privacy through anonymized differential features and role-restricted dashboard access.
Recommend targeted remedial modules matching specific conceptual weak points.

title: Neural Collaborative Course & Project Recommender
summary: A graph neural network architecture suggesting personalized elective courses, research papers, and cross-departmental hackathon teammates based on skills and aspirations.
overview: The Neural Collaborative Recommender constructs a heterogeneous academic knowledge graph connecting students, elective courses, github repositories, research publications, and skill taxonomies. Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) learn relational node embeddings that power recommendations with superior serendipity and relevance.
problem: Students select final-year capstones and open electives with limited visibility, often duplicating previous student efforts or missing complementary teammates across different SIET branches.
solution: We deployed LightGCN and GraphSAGE models using PyTorch Geometric, caching top-K neighborhood rankings in Redis for sub-50ms user query resolution.
objectives: Break departmental academic silos by matching complementary skill sets for national hackathons.
Generate personalized reading lists connecting lecture concepts with state-of-the-art conference papers.
Achieve high recommendation diversity while keeping NDCG@10 above 0.42.

title: AI-Powered Urban Traffic & Congestion Analyzer
summary: Real-time traffic flow prediction, density estimation, and emergency vehicle green-corridor management using deep convolutional networks.
overview: Urban bottlenecks in industrial corridors cause significant fuel waste and delays for emergency response vehicles. This project couples roadside CCTV streams with deep vehicle counting and velocity estimators to dynamically calculate traffic signal phase durations.
problem: Static timer-based traffic signals fail to adapt during peak morning hours and cannot yield priority to approaching ambulances.
solution: A distributed visual pipeline feeds vehicle density metrics into a reinforcement learning controller that adjusts traffic light cycles in real-time.
objectives: Reduce average intersection waiting time by 28% across arterial corridors.
Guarantee automatic green corridor preemption when emergency sirens or flashing beacons are verified.

title: Automated Code Review & Bug Sentinel
summary: An intelligent static analysis and neural code comprehension engine flagging security vulnerabilities and recommending idiomatic code refactors.
overview: An automated GitHub Actions and GitLab CI companion that parses abstract syntax trees, checks for OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities, and utilizes fine-tuned CodeLlama models to generate inline code reviews and unit test stubs for student projects.
problem: Student code repositories frequently contain unvalidated user inputs, hardcoded secrets, and inefficient algorithms that go unnoticed due to faculty grading constraints.
solution: We unified AST security rules with transformer-based reasoning to comment directly on Pull Requests with suggested one-click fixes.
objectives: Catch 95% of common security and concurrency defects before student submissions.
Foster software engineering best practices within the student developer community.
